title: Drishyam 3 Ends Overseas Run at Rs 144.89 Crore, Ninth-Biggest Bollywood Grosser Abroad Post-COVID
excerpt: Ajay Devgn's crime thriller closed its international run as his biggest overseas grosser ever, with North America contributing an estimated $6.72 million, according to Koimoi's tracking.
body:
• Drishyam 3 has ended its overseas run with an estimated Rs 144.89 crore gross, according to Koimoi's box-office tracking — Bollywood's ninth-highest overseas gross of the post-COVID era.
  • North America was its biggest market at an estimated $6.72 million (Rs 63.2 crore), followed by Australia at A$2.55 million (Rs 16.44 crore) and the UK at £1.11 million (Rs 13.93 crore).
  • It is Ajay Devgn's highest-grossing film overseas, passing Singham Again (Rs 82.96 crore) by a wide margin, and it nudged past Stree 2 (Rs 144 crore) for ninth place on the post-COVID list.
  • With India grosses added, Koimoi puts the worldwide total at Rs 592.98 crore after 36 days; tracker Sacnilk's worldwide estimate is lower, at Rs 587.42 crore.

The overseas run of Drishyam 3 is over, and the Hindi crime thriller has closed it with numbers nobody predicted for the genre. Koimoi's box-office tracking puts the film's final overseas gross at an estimated Rs 144.89 crore — good enough for ninth place among Bollywood films at the overseas box office in the post-COVID era, and the biggest international result of Ajay Devgn's career.

Drishyam 3, directed by Abhishek Pathak and starring Devgn as Vijay Salgaonkar alongside Tabu and Jaideep Ahlawat, released in theatres on October 2, 2026. It is the third film in the Hindi Drishyam series — a franchise that began as a remake of the Malayalam original — and it arrived with the kind of pre-release interest that usually belongs to action spectacles, not slow-burn thrillers.

Where the money came from

North America (the US and Canada) delivered the largest share, an estimated $6.72 million (Rs 63.2 crore) — the diaspora market doing the heavy lifting for a Hindi-language thriller. Australia contributed an estimated A$2.55 million (Rs 16.44 crore) and the United Kingdom £1.11 million (Rs 13.93 crore), with the balance from other territories, according to Koimoi's territory breakdown.

For Devgn, the film replaces Singham Again (Rs 82.96 crore overseas) as his biggest international grosser, ahead of it by Rs 61.93 crore. On the post-COVID overseas list, Drishyam 3's Rs 144.89 crore edges Stree 2 (Rs 144 crore) for ninth place and sits behind Rocky Aur Rani Kii Prem Kahaani (Rs 168 crore); the list is topped by Dhurandhar 2 at Rs 451 crore, followed by Pathaan (Rs 412 crore) and Jawan (Rs 406 crore).

"For Devgn, the film replaces Singham Again (Rs 82.96 crore overseas) as his biggest international grosser, ahead of it by Rs 61.93 crore."

The full picture

At home, Koimoi's day-wise tracker puts the film at Rs 379.7 crore net (Rs 448.09 crore gross) in India after 36 days, for a worldwide gross of Rs 592.98 crore. Box-office trackers do not always agree: Sacnilk's tally for the same period is Rs 587.42 crore worldwide, with a lower overseas figure of Rs 133.20 crore. Both trackers describe estimates compiled from trade sources rather than audited figures.

The run caps an exceptional few weeks for the franchise. As we reported earlier, the film also finished its run on BookMyShow as Bollywood's tenth-highest ticket-seller ever on the platform. For US and Canadian readers, the theatrical run has ended in most markets; a streaming date has not been announced in the sources reporting the box-office close.
